From 32594b09854970d7ba83eb2dc8c69a2edd158c8e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 19:21:05 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] inet: frags: fix use-after-free caused by the
 fqdir_pre_exit() flush

On netns teardown, fqdir_pre_exit() walks the fqdir rhashtable and
flushes every fragment queue that is not yet complete using
inet_frag_queue_flush(). That helper frees all the skbs queued on the
fragment queue but does not set INET_FRAG_COMPLETE, and leaves
q->fragments_tail and q->last_run_head pointing at the freed skbs.
The queue itself stays in the rhashtable.

fqdir_pre_exit() first lowers high_thresh to 0 to stop new queue lookups,
but it cannot stop a fragment that already obtained the queue through
inet_frag_find() earlier and stalled just before taking the queue lock.
Once that fragment resumes after the flush and takes the queue lock,
it passes the INET_FRAG_COMPLETE check and then dereferences the freed
fragments_tail. inet_frag_queue_insert() reads FRAG_CB() and ->len of
that pointer and, on the append path, writes ->next_frag, causing a
slab use-after-free. IPv6, nf_conntrack_reasm6 and 6lowpan reassembly
share the same flush path and are affected as well.

Reset rb_fragments, fragments_tail and last_run_head in
inet_frag_queue_flush() so a flushed queue no longer points at the
freed skbs. A fragment that resumes after the flush and takes the
queue lock then finds an empty queue and starts a new run instead of
dereferencing the freed fragments_tail. ip_frag_reinit() already
performed this reset after its own flush, so drop the now duplicate
code there.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 006a5035b495 ("inet: frags: flush pending skbs in fqdir_pre_exit()")
Suggested-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Hyunwoo Kim <imv4bel@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/ah6ukYq5G98LshdA@v4bel
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/ipv4/inet_fragment.c b/net/ipv4/inet_fragment.c
index 393770920abd..1127519b8416 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/inet_fragment.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/inet_fragment.c
@@ -328,6 +328,9 @@ void inet_frag_queue_flush(struct inet_frag_queue *q,
 	reason = reason ?: SKB_DROP_REASON_FRAG_REASM_TIMEOUT;
 	sum = inet_frag_rbtree_purge(&q->rb_fragments, reason);
 	sub_frag_mem_limit(q->fqdir, sum);
+	q->rb_fragments = RB_ROOT;
+	q->fragments_tail = NULL;
+	q->last_run_head = NULL;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(inet_frag_queue_flush);
 

diff --git a/net/ipv4/ip_fragment.c b/net/ipv4/ip_fragment.c
index 56b0f738d2f2..c790d2f49487 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/ip_fragment.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/ip_fragment.c
@@ -250,9 +250,6 @@ static int ip_frag_reinit(struct ipq *qp)
 	qp->q.flags = 0;
 	qp->q.len = 0;
 	qp->q.meat = 0;
-	qp->q.rb_fragments = RB_ROOT;
-	qp->q.fragments_tail = NULL;
-	qp->q.last_run_head = NULL;
 	qp->iif = 0;
 	qp->ecn = 0;
 
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a use-after-free vulnerability in the IPv4/IPv6 fragment reassembly code during network namespace teardown. The race occurs because `fqdir_pre_exit()` flushes fragment queues without clearing pointers to freed skbs, allowing a concurrent fragment lookup to dereference freed memory.

**Changes made:**

1. **`net/ipv4/inet_fragment.c` – `inet_frag_queue_flush()`**:  
   After purging the rbtree of fragment skbs, the function now resets `q->rb_fragments` to `RB_ROOT`, `q->fragments_tail` to `NULL`, and `q->last_run_head` to `NULL`. This ensures that any queue that has been flushed no longer holds stale pointers to freed skbs.

2. **`net/ipv4/ip_fragment.c` – `ip_frag_reinit()`**:  
   Removed the three lines that previously reset `rb_fragments`, `fragments_tail`, and `last_run_head` because `inet_frag_queue_flush()` (which is called earlier in the same function) now performs those resets. This eliminates duplicate code and ensures consistency.

**Relationship between changes:**  
The primary fix is in the common flush helper (`inet_frag_queue_flush()`), which is used by all reassembly variants (IPv4, IPv6, nf_conntrack_reasm6, 6lowpan). By resetting the queue pointers there, the race condition is prevented regardless of the caller. The removal of redundant resets in `ip_frag_reinit()` avoids a double reset and makes the code cleaner, relying on the single point of truth in the shared flush function.

This patch fixes a use-after-free vulnerability caused by a race condition during network namespace teardown. The issue occurs in the fragment queue flushing path (`inet_frag_queue_flush`) which does not reset queue metadata after freeing skbs, allowing a concurrent fragment to later access freed memory.

### Modifications per file

1. **`net/ipv4/inet_fragment.c`** (function `inet_frag_queue_flush`):
   - After purging the fragment queue's rbtree and updating memory counters, the function now resets three queue fields:
     - `q->rb_fragments = RB_ROOT;`
     - `q->fragments_tail = NULL;`
     - `q->last_run_head = NULL;`
   - This ensures that after flushing, the queue no longer holds pointers to the freed skbs.

2. **`net/ipv4/ip_fragment.c`** (function `ip_frag_reinit`):
   - Removed the three lines that previously reset the same fields (`rb_fragments`, `fragments_tail`, `last_run_head`), as this reset is now performed in `inet_frag_queue_flush`, which is called before `ip_frag_reinit` in the relevant code paths.

- The core fix is in `inet_frag_queue_flush` (file 1): by resetting queue pointers after flushing, the queue appears empty to any fragment operation that resumes later. This prevents a stalled fragment from dereferencing stale pointers.
- The removal in `ip_frag_reinit` (file 2) is a cleanup of now-duplicate code, since `ip_frag_reinit` is always called after a flush that already performs the reset. The two changes are tightly coupled: the reset is moved to the common flush routine to cover all callers (including `fqdir_pre_exit`), and the duplicate in the IPv4-specific reinit function is eliminated to avoid redundancy and maintain consistency.

The patch addresses a use-after-free vulnerability in the inet fragment handling subsystem during network namespace teardown. It modifies the flush path to reset critical pointers after freeing skbs, and removes a redundant reset from a specific caller.

## Modifications in Each File

### `net/ipv4/inet_fragment.c`
- In `inet_frag_queue_flush()`, three lines are added after the `inet_frag_rbtree_purge()` and `sub_frag_mem_limit()` calls:
  - `q->rb_fragments = RB_ROOT;`
  - `q->fragments_tail = NULL;`
  - `q->last_run_head = NULL;`
- This ensures that after all skbs in the fragment queue are purged, the queue no longer holds dangling pointers to freed memory.

### `net/ipv4/ip_fragment.c`
- In `ip_frag_reinit()`, the three lines that previously performed the same reset are removed:
  - ~~`qp->q.rb_fragments = RB_ROOT;`~~
  - ~~`qp->q.fragments_tail = NULL;`~~
  - ~~`qp->q.last_run_head = NULL;`~~
- This removal avoids duplication, since the reset is now handled in the common `inet_frag_queue_flush()` function.

## Relationships Between the Modifications

- **Common flush path**: The reset of `rb_fragments`, `fragments_tail`, and `last_run_head` is moved from the specific `ip_frag_reinit()` function into the shared `inet_frag_queue_flush()` function. This function is called:
  - Internally by `fqdir_pre_exit()` during netns teardown (the original bug context).
  - Also by `ip_frag_reinit()` during IPv4 fragment reassembly reinitialization.
- **Bug cause and fix**: During `fqdir_pre_exit()`, queues are flushed but not marked as complete, leaving the pointers referencing the now-freed skbs. A concurrent fragment operation that obtained the queue before the flush but stalled can later take the queue lock, see the empty queue (INET_FRAG_COMPLETE not set), and then dereference the stale `fragments_tail`. By clearing these pointers in the flush, such a concurrent operation will find an empty queue and start fresh, preventing use-after-free.
- **Code deduplication**: Since `inet_frag_queue_flush()` now performs the reset, the identical reset code in `ip_frag_reinit()` is no longer needed and is removed, maintaining consistency across all flush call sites.

Here is the root cause:
The function `fqdir_pre_exit()` calls `inet_frag_queue_flush()` which frees all skbs in a fragment queue but does not reset the queue's `rb_fragments`, `fragments_tail`, and `last_run_head` pointers, and does not set `INET_FRAG_COMPLETE`. A concurrent fragment operation that obtained the queue before the flush but stalled can later resume, take the lock, check `INET_FRAG_COMPLETE` (still not set), and then dereference the now-freed `fragments_tail` pointer, leading to a use-after-free.

Here is the patch:
 
 void inet_frag_queue_flush(struct inet_frag_queue *q,
 			   enum skb_drop_reason reason)
 {
 	unsigned int sum;
 
 	reason = reason ?: SKB_DROP_REASON_FRAG_REASM_TIMEOUT;
 	sum = inet_frag_rbtree_purge(&q->rb_fragments, reason);
 	sub_frag_mem_limit(q->fqdir, sum);
+	q->rb_fragments = RB_ROOT;
+	q->fragments_tail = NULL;
+	q->last_run_head = NULL;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(inet_frag_queue_flush);
